info.title: RawEval LLM Call Host
info.description:
**RawEval LLM Call Host** - Enterprise-grade multi-model LLM orchestration system.
    
    ## Features
    
    - **Multi-Provider Support**: OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, OpenRouter
    - **14+ Workflow Types**: Single model, multi-model comparison, parallel processing, file processing, research, code analysis, and more
    - **File Processing**: PDF, CSV, JSON, images, audio, video
    - **Batch Operations**: Execute multiple LLM calls in parallel or sequentially
    - **Advanced Workflows**: LangGraph integration, multithreading support
    - **Comprehensive Logging**: Request/response tracking and error handling
    
    ## Quick Start
    
    1. Set environment variables (API keys for providers)
    2. Start the service: `make llm-host-dev`
    3. Access API docs: http://localhost:8002/docs
    
    ## Workflow Types
    
    - `single_model`: Execute one model
    - `multi_model_comparison`: Compare multiple models sequentially
    - `parallel_processing`: Execute multiple models in parallel
    - `file_processing`: Process files with LLM analysis
    - `autograder`: Grade submissions with rubric
    - `research`: Multi-step research workflow
    - `code_analysis`: Code review workflow
    - `sentiment_analysis`: Analyze sentiment
    - `summarization`: Create summaries
    - `translation`: Translate text
    - `classification`: Categorize content
    - `qa_generation`: Generate Q&A pairs
    - `dynamic_model_call`: Direct model call
    
    ## Performance
    
    - Single model latency: <2000ms
    - Multi-model parallel: <5000ms
    - Batch processing: <30000ms (5 requests)

get.description:
Check the health status of the LLM Call Host service.
    
    Returns:
    - Service status (healthy/unhealthy)
    - List of available LLM providers
    - Service version and timestamp
    
    Use this endpoint for monitoring and load balancer health checks.

200.description: Service health status with available providers

post.description:
Upload files that will be used in LLM calls.
    
    Files are uploaded to S3 and return S3 keys/URLs that can be used in workflow requests.
    
    ## Supported File Types:
    - PDF, CSV, JSON, images, video, audio, text files
    - Max file size: 100MB per file

200.description: File upload information with S3 keys and URLs

post.description:
Execute a workflow-based LLM call with support for 14+ workflow types.
    
    ## Supported Workflow Types:
    
    - **single_model**: Execute one model call (fastest, lowest cost)
    - **multi_model_comparison**: Compare multiple models sequentially (best quality)
    - **parallel_processing**: Execute multiple models in parallel (fastest for multiple models)
    - **file_processing**: Process files (PDF, CSV, images) with LLM analysis
    - **autograder**: Grade submissions with rubric
    - **research**: Multi-step research workflow
    - **code_analysis**: Code review workflow
    - **sentiment_analysis**: Analyze sentiment
    - **summarization**: Create summaries
    - **translation**: Translate text
    - **classification**: Categorize content
    - **qa_generation**: Generate Q&A pairs
    - **dynamic_model_call**: Direct model call
    
    ## Performance:
    
    - Single model: 500-2000ms
    - Multi-model comparison: 2000-5000ms
    - Parallel processing: 1000-3000ms
    - File processing: 3000-10000ms
    
    ## File Processing:
    
    Supports: PDF, CSV, JSON, images, video, audio, text files
    Max file size: 100MB
    
    ## Conversation Support:
    
    - **New Session**: Omit `session_id` and `request_id` to create a new conversation
    - **Continue Session**: Provide `session_id` or `request_id` to continue an existing conversation
    - **Conversation History**: All messages (user, system, assistant) are stored and can be retrieved
    - **Multi-turn**: Support for multiple back-and-forth exchanges in a single session

Execute a direct LLM call without workflow overhead.
    
    This is the fastest way to get a response from a single LLM model.
    Perfect for simple queries that don't require multi-model comparison or file processing.
    
    ## Supported Providers:
    
    - OpenAI (gpt-4o, gpt-4-turbo, o1, o3)
    - Claude (claude-3-5-sonnet, claude-3-opus, claude-3-haiku)
    - Gemini (gemini-2.0-pro, gemini-2.0-flash, gemini-1.5-pro)
    - Grok (grok-3, grok-2-vision)
    - DeepSeek (deepseek-chat, deepseek-coder)
    - OpenRouter (meta-llama/llama-3.1-70b, meta-llama/llama-2-70b)
    
    ## Performance:
    
    - Typical latency: 500-2000ms
    - Timeout: 120 seconds
    
    ## Parameters:
    
    - **temperature**: Controls randomness (0.0-2.0, default: 0.7)
    - **max_tokens**: Maximum tokens to generate
    - **top_p**: Nucleus sampling parameter
    - **frequency_penalty**: Reduce repetition (-2.0 to 2.0)
    - **presence_penalty**: Encourage new topics (-2.0 to 2.0)

Execute multiple LLM calls in a single request.
    
    ## Execution Modes:
    
    - **Parallel** (`parallel: true`): All requests execute simultaneously
      - Faster: Total time = max(individual latencies)
      - Best for: Independent requests, speed-critical operations
      - Max concurrent: 5 requests
    
    - **Sequential** (`parallel: false`): Requests execute one after another
      - Slower: Total time = sum(individual latencies)
      - Best for: Dependent requests, cost optimization
    
    ## Use Cases:
    
    - Process multiple prompts with different models
    - Compare responses across providers
    - Bulk data processing
    - A/B testing model configurations
    
    ## Performance:
    
    - Parallel batch (5 requests): 2000-5000ms
    - Sequential batch (5 requests): 5000-10000ms
    - Timeout: 180 seconds (3 minutes)
    
    ## Limits:
    
    - Max batch size: 5 requests
    - Max timeout: 180 seconds

400.description: Invalid batch request (too many requests, invalid parameters)

get.description:
Get the current status of a workflow or LLM call request.
    
    ## Status Values:
    
    - **pending**: Request queued, not yet started
    - **in_progress**: Request currently executing
    - **completed**: Request finished successfully
    - **failed**: Request failed with error
    - **partial**: Some models succeeded, some failed
    
    ## Use Cases:
    
    - Poll for long-running workflow completion
    - Monitor batch processing progress
    - Check if request is still processing
    - Get attachment information
    
    **Note**: Request status is stored in database for persistent tracking.

schema.title: Response Get Status Status  Request Id  Get

get.description:
Retrieve the complete results of a finished workflow or LLM call.
    
    ## Response Includes:
    
    - All model responses with content
    - Token usage statistics
    - Latency metrics per model
    - Error information (if any)
    - Metadata and timestamps
    - File attachments information
    
    ## Use Cases:
    
    - Retrieve results after async workflow completion
    - Analyze model performance metrics
    - Compare responses across models
    - Export results for further processing
    - Access file attachments and S3 locations
    
    **Note**: Results are stored in database and memory cache.

404.description: Request ID not found or results not available

post.description:
Receive webhook callbacks for long-running workflows.
    
    ## Use Cases:
    
    - Notify external systems when workflows complete
    - Integrate with third-party services
    - Trigger downstream processes
    - Update external databases
    
    ## Callback Payload:
    
    The callback will include:
    - Request ID
    - Workflow status
    - Results summary
    - Error information (if any)
    - Timestamps
    
    **Note**: This is a placeholder endpoint. Full webhook support
    will be implemented in future versions.

get.description:
Get the complete conversation history for a session.
    
    Returns all messages in the conversation including user prompts,
    system messages, and assistant responses with their metadata.

Get all file attachments for a specific LLM call session.
    
    Returns detailed information about all files attached to a request,
    including S3 locations, file types, and sizes.

Welcome endpoint with API information and available endpoints.
    
    Returns basic service information and links to documentation.
